PG.rationale: PG's fundamental trajectory has deteriorated sharply: operating margin has compressed 460bp in two quarters (26.2% → 24.2% → 21.6%), driven by a 76% surge in WTI crude to $108.64/bbl that is directly pressuring petrochemical and logistics costs. Gross margin has fallen to 49.5% from 51.4% in Q1, and management projects a $1 billion after-tax annual headwind if Brent stays near $100. Sequential revenue and EPS are declining (-4.4% and -8.4% QoQ respectively), and while YoY growth remains positive, the three-quarter sequential softening trend is clear. Valuation at 23.1x PE is near the floor of its 1-year range but is justified by the margin deterioration — the earnings yield of 4.3% now sits below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.4%, removing the defensive yield rationale. The stock is 14% below its 52-week high with no capitulation or overshoot. Volume growth in Q3 (2%) is a positive but is one quarter old and fragile against consumer price fatigue and private label encroachment. Management is guiding toward the lower end of its FY2026 range ($6.83–$7.09 core EPS). Insider selling post-earnings (Executive Chairman $28M, CBO $14.5M) signals lack of conviction. The restructuring (7,000 job cuts) and innovation pipeline (Tide EVO, Pampers Prestige) are structural positives but are multi-year stories that cannot offset the near-term margin headwind. With oil unresolved, margins compressing, and no credible near-term catalyst for re-rating, the risk-reward is unfavorable.
key_factors: Operating margin compression: 26.2% (Q1 FY2026) → 24.2% (Q2) → 21.6% (Q3), a 460bp decline in two quarters driven by input cost pressures
WTI crude surged 76% from $61.60/bbl (Feb 2026) to $108.64/bbl (Apr 2026), directly pressuring PG's petrochemical, packaging, and logistics costs
Gross margin eroded from 51.4% (Q1) to 49.5% (Q3), a 150bp YoY contraction despite higher revenue, indicating pricing power limits
CFO disclosed $1 billion annual after-tax headwind if Brent crude stays near $100/barrel; tariff-specific impact ~$400M for FY2026
Sequential revenue -4.4% and EPS -8.4% in Q3 vs Q2, extending three-quarter softening trend from Q1 peak of $22.39B
PE diluted at 23.1x near 1-year floor (21.7x–26.7x range) but justified by margin trajectory; earnings yield 4.3% below 10-year Treasury yield 4.4%
Stock at $147.09, down 14% from 52-week high of $170.99, with three consecutive quarterly price declines
FY2026 guidance maintained at organic sales flat to +4% and core EPS $6.83–$7.09, but management signaling lower end due to tariff and commodity headwinds
Volume growth of 2% in Q3 (first in a year) is positive but fragile; Beauty standout at 5% volume growth while Grooming and Health Care declined 2%
Insider selling post-earnings: Executive Chairman Jon Moeller ($28M), Chief Brand Officer Marc Pritchard ($14.5M)
Restructuring plan to cut ~7,000 non-manufacturing jobs by mid-2027 is a multi-year structural positive but not a near-term catalyst
ROE 29.7% and cash conversion 1.02x (OCF/NI) remain healthy, providing fundamental quality anchor but insufficient to offset margin headwinds
